summary.text: A 36-year-old Sudanese male proband had hypohidrosis, hypotrichosis and hypodontia, with recurrent hyperthermia in hot weather, light and dry scalp hair, prominent ears, protruding lips, ichthyosis on the legs, dry skin and sole hyperkeratosis. Symptoms were present since birth; a dental evaluation in 2012 raised clinical suspicion of hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia, and molecular testing was performed in 2014 after referral to a genetic center.

Intraoral examination showed a missing deciduous upper left lateral incisor and a primary second molar, and an orthopantomogram showed no permanent successor. Mental and physical development was normal with no nail abnormalities. EDA exons were sequenced for the proband and five relatives with no mutation found; the authors presumed a possible X-linked pattern without ruling out a de novo mutation, and he was clinically diagnosed with hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia with no EDA gene mutation.

No specific therapy was provided. He was advised on behavioral and environmental changes to avoid overheating and referred to genetic counseling, and exome sequencing is recommended. No complications or progression were reported and he remained stable with avoidance of thermal triggers, hydration and skin moisturization; the patient is deceased, with time and cause not stated.
